Hey @pcbeingused333, thank you for your contribution!

The fork part should land. Since #4449, `close()` takes the handler lock before `_checkpid()`. Also, a child forked during a MOVING keeps the temporary host and relaxed timeouts forever, because the timers that would revert them do not exist in the child. Please keep reverting right away in the child: a MOVING that is still active is sent again to the new connections.

Please drop the second part: the `_closed` flag, `reopen()` and the `_on_reuse()` calls in `get_connection()` on both stacks. A late MOVING on a closed pool already reverts when its timer fires. The flag adds a check to every `get_connection()` and the next call clears it, even a failing one, so it only partly closes the window. Its reuse test also fails on the hiredis jobs. Once only the fork reset and its tests remain, I will take another look.

Thanks for the update, the scope looks right now.

One blocking point remains. `reset_after_fork()` replaces the handler lock, but `cancel_scheduled_tasks()` then calls `handle_node_moved_notification()`, which takes `self.pool._lock`, and `reset()` does not replace that lock. The parent paths that hold the handler lock during a MOVING (the handling block, `run_proactive_reconnect()` and the timer cleanup) also hold `pool._lock`. So a child forked at that point still hangs, now inside `_checkpid()`. Please replace the pool lock in the fork branch of `reset()` before the handler reset, on both pool classes. Please also add a test where the parent thread holds `pool._lock` while a handoff is pending.

Thanks for the updates. The pool lock replacement, the maintenance flag reset and the new fork tests look good.

One window is still open. In `handle_node_moving_notification()`, `update_connection_kwargs()` runs before `_pending_handoffs.add()`. If the process forks while the thread holding the handler lock is between the two, `reset_after_fork()` cancels the timer but has no handoff to clean up, and the child keeps the temporary host and relaxed timeouts. Please revert any MOVING kwargs still on the pool after `cancel_scheduled_tasks()` in `reset_after_fork()`, only when `maintenance_state` is `MOVING`. Please also add a test that applies the MOVING kwargs with no pending handoff and checks that a fork reset restores the original host and timeouts.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid inherited pool locks during fork reset**

When a `BlockingConnectionPool` forks while another parent thread holds `pool._lock` and a MOVING handoff is pending, this new call reaches `handle_node_moved_notification()`, which tries to acquire that inherited lock. The parent thread cannot release it in the child, so `_checkpid()` deadlocks before the pool can serve a new connection (the normal non-maintenance blocking acquisition would not otherwise take `_lock`). Reinitialize the pool lock before this cleanup, or restore the inherited notification state without acquiring it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reopen the handler only after reserving a connection**

On a closed pool whose only slot is still checked out, this clears `_closed` before `make_connection()` can raise `MaxConnectionsError` (and the Blocking variants clear it before a wait can time out). If the outstanding connection then reads a MOVING, the handler accepts it and sync `_schedule()` starts another non-daemon timer even though no connection was returned and no subsequent close is guaranteed, recreating the shutdown-until-TTL and temporary-kwargs regression. Clear the flag only after a slot has actually been reserved; the two async acquisition paths have the same premature reopen.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore kwargs when forking before handoff registration**

When the process forks while another thread is between `update_connection_kwargs()` and `_pending_handoffs.add()` (including the timer-start window in `_schedule()`), the child reaches this call with the temporary host/timeouts applied but no registered cleanup. `cancel_scheduled_tasks()` can cancel an already-created timer, but its cleanup loop has no notification to restore the kwargs, and clearing `_processed_notifications` does not restore them; a child that does not receive a redelivery before the TTL will keep creating connections to the temporary endpoint. Restore the MOVING kwargs independently of `_pending_handoffs`, or register the handoff before mutating them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear inherited maintenance mode during blocking-pool reset**

When a `BlockingConnectionPool` forks while `handle_node_moving_notification()` is between `set_in_maintenance(True)` and the matching `False`, this branch replaces the inherited lock but leaves `_in_maintenance=True`. The child's first checkout then acquires the new RLock, and nested `make_connection()` clears the shared `_locked` flag after releasing only its recursive acquisition, so the outer checkout never releases its acquisition; any later pool access from another child thread blocks forever. Reset `_in_maintenance` and the lock bookkeeping along with `_lock`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel the parent timer before leaving the fork test**

When this test reaches the parent-side `finally`, the `handle_notification(... ttl=60)` call above has started a non-daemon `threading.Timer`; only the forked child calls `pool.close()`, so the parent never cancels it. Running this test alone reports both parametrizations passing in about 0.5 seconds but leaves pytest alive until the 60-second timers fire (a 20-second run exited via timeout), so close the parent pool in this `finally`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

### Fork leaves pool in maintenance mode **Medium Severity** `BlockingConnectionPool.reset()` replaces `_lock` after a fork but never clears `_in_maintenance`. That flag is True while the parent holds the pool lock during MOVING apply, so a forked child can inherit it. `get_connection` then nests `make_connection`; both acquire `_lock` and the inner `finally` drops `_locked`, leaking the lock so other threads block.
Additional Locations (2) - [`redis/maint_notifications.py#L886-L889`](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/6ce10e37fcfbc7acfa843b109e42f0fa6c18a298/redis/maint_notifications.py#L886-L889) - [`redis/connection.py#L4564-L4565`](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/6ce10e37fcfbc7acfa843b109e42f0fa6c18a298/redis/connection.py#L4564-L4565)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6ce10e37fcfbc7acfa843b109e42f0fa6c18a298. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Settle in-flight completion events during fork reset**

When the process forks after a parent cleanup has removed a notification from `_pending_handoffs` but before `MaintenanceCompletedEvent` reaches every listener (for example, while an earlier listener is still running), the child inherits listeners' started state but this call finds no pending handoff and emits no completion before the remaining bookkeeping is cleared. A stateful `MaintNotificationsConfig.event_dispatcher` listener that relies on the documented event pair can consequently remain relaxed indefinitely in the child, so the fork reset also needs to settle handoffs whose completion dispatch is still in flight.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L92-L92](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/2aee18ee6f830dc7d16a56b1e97b22751c226802/AGENTS.md#L92-L92)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid inherited locks in fork-only cleanup**

When a fork occurs while a scheduled `threading.Timer`'s `finished` condition or the configured `EventDispatcher._lock` is owned by another parent thread, this new reset call still acquires those inherited locks: `cancel_scheduled_tasks()` invokes `Timer.cancel()` and, for a pending relaxed handoff, synchronously emits the completion event. Those owners no longer exist, so the child's first checkout/`_checkpid()` can hang indefinitely despite replacing the pool and handler locks; use fork-only cleanup that drops the timer objects and reinitializes or avoids dispatcher synchronization instead of normal close-time cancellation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L92-L92](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/aeea7c15b7ae39e2332fed41ca95f86562504bac/AGENTS.md#L92-L92)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Declining: both locks are only held momentarily by their owners (`Timer.finished` around `wait()` entry/exit and `set()`, `EventDispatcher._lock` only while snapshotting listeners, never across a listener call). A fork landing inside those windows is the general fork-with-threads hazard that applies to every stdlib lock, not something this reset introduces.

New test `test_pool_close_in_forked_child_does_not_block_on_inherited_pool_lock` (both pool classes): a parent thread holds `pool._lock` while a handoff is pending, the process forks, and the child closes the pool under a 5 s alarm; it fails on the previous head and passes now.

The first one is for the review bots' follow-up finding (Codex P1 / Cursor Bugbot): `BlockingConnectionPool.reset()` replaced the inherited lock in the fork branch but left `_in_maintenance` (and `_locked`) as the parent had them. The parent thread that would clear them does not exist in the child, so the child's first checkout nested on the new `RLock` and leaked it. The fork branch now clears both flags; `test_blocking_pool_fork_in_maintenance_does_not_stay_in_maintenance` fails without it.

Also closed the parent pool at the end of the earlier fork test so its MOVING timer no longer keeps pytest alive (Codex P2).

New test `test_pool_reset_in_forked_child_restores_moving_kwargs_without_pending_handoff` applies the MOVING kwargs with no pending handoff and checks that a fork reset restores the original host and timeouts (fails without the change, passes with it).
